Subject: Reseed plan: phased waves + validation/fallback workflow

Hey Elena and Chris —

Following our call this morning, attaching a compact wave plan for the index reseed and a short checklist for rerank smoke testing. The goal is to avoid a monolithic backfill and give BrightMart safe rollback/fallback semantics if we see quality drift during a wave.

High level approach: 
- Small seed wave (1% of corpus) with rerank baseline checks and latched read-only traffic.
- Canary wave (10%) with A/B traffic and targeted user segments.
- Bulk fill waves (25% each) with automated KV prefix caching and incremental priming.

Requests for you: 
1) Confirm priority content types for the first two waves (product pages, help articles, user-generated reviews).
2) Share any existing blacklist/skip rules we should honor during reseed.
3) Approve the proposed smoke test window: 30-minute golden queries + 1000-sample rerank QA per wave.

Attachments: reseed_wave_plan.xlsx; rerank-smoke-tests.md

I'll loop Ben for operational runbook details and Marissa for CSM acceptance gates. Karthik will own DB compatibility checks and fallback mappings to current vector-store.

Thanks —
Stephanie Nguyen
Sr. Customer Solutions, Redwood Inference
stephanie@redwood.com

Thanks Stephanie — this looks sane. A few clarifying Qs from ops: 

1) Can the canary wave be scoped to only queries that hit the new index (so we avoid noisy samples)?
2) For the 1000-sample rerank QA, do you mean 1000 end-to-end requests or 1000 pairs (original vs candidate)?
3) What's the expected delta in storage/IO while the bulk fill runs — we want to plan a maintenance window for our DB replicas.

Happy to align on a short ops sync tomorrow. Elena, do you have the priority content list?

—Chris

Subject: Re: Reseed plan: phased waves + validation/fallback workflow

Team — operational notes and proposed owners below. Quoting Elena's ask re: canary scoping and sample counts.

- Canary scoping: yes, we can route ~5% of read traffic that matches the new-index prefix to the canary. That prevents unrelated query churn. (Will require a short config push to the routing policy.)
- Sample definition: we will run 1000 E2E queries and compute: precision@10, reciprocal rank delta, and order-overlap (Jaccard) between old and new top-20.

Owners: 
- Runbook and cut timing: Ben Carter (ops lead). Attachment: index-consistency-checklist.pdf (will be the step-by-step).
- Rerank smoke harness: Karthik Iyer (rerank tests + metrics). Artifact: rerank-smoke-tests.md
- CSM acceptance & communication: Marissa Cole (customer-facing readiness + incident playbook).

Fallback workflow (brief): 
1) If precision@10 drops more than 5% vs baseline during any wave, we automatically flip read traffic back to the previous index variant for that segment.
2) If order-overlap < 0.6 on critical golden queries, we pause the wave and run a targeted seed-without-read test to isolate indexing errors.
3) After an automated rollback, we capture the rerank logs and kick a post-mortem with BrightMart within 48h.

I'll schedule the ops sync and put the runbook in the shared Drive.

Ben

Notes: we validated that Atlas Search will not need schema changes for the new vectors, but we will run a shrink/compact after each bulk wave to manage IO. Chris, please confirm replica maintenance timing — Ben flagged potential extra IO during the compact.
